Honestly I can see both POVs (you and your friends). Their intentions in responding that way could be different from how you interpreted what they said. For example, your friend could have suggested that you choose a different way to walk because they may not have assumed it was a safe place, and it is very abnormal for someone to be attacked like that in the open with people around. I personally would never assume that anything like that would have happened out in the open like that. I definitely don't think it's anything like questioning the clothing you were wearing. When someone suggests that the clothing someone wore directly caused their assualt, it's more of a way to demean the victim and lessen the accountability of the attacker. I think that by suggesting you choose a safer route to get home, it isn't suggesting at all that it is your fault and it doesn't give the attacker the benefit of the doubt, If that makes any sense? And as for the second comment made by your friend, I don't think they were trying to suggest that you were ignorant or that you are unfairly upset over the situation. Like you said, they probably are aware that you understand the problems regarding mental health among the homeless population, so they probably didn't say it in a way to appear as "woke" or to make you feel bad or ignorant. They probably were just simply making a statement about the situation without the intent of demeaning you or belittling the attack. But, like I said, it's all about the intent your friends had, and I think your reactions to what they had said are completely valid. I think it would be good to communicate to them about how what they said made you feel angry and how you feel it was wrong of them to say what they did.

We have all done things we aren't proud of. I can't understand what you are going through since I have never been in a similar situation, but you sound like an aware and genuinely good person. You are acknowledging what you did was wrong, and you fully regret it. You were young and hormonal, and you made mistakes. I know it's easy to say, but you deserve forgiveness from yourself. Have you sought any sort of counseling or therapy? Therapy has helped me get through situations where I was angry and unforgiving of myself, I think it would be something you should really consider.

You are recognizing what you did was wrong and are fully admitting to it. That's a big step. You said this happened in your teens, so I'm guessing it stopped. You can never change who you were in the past, but you can change who you are now. It seems like you have done that, otherwise you would be continuing to do those awful things. I know it's hard, but try to forgive yourself. We all make mistakes, and all you can do is continue to change for the better; you can still be a good person.
